slides.title: Heartbreak is one of the biggest [[p*rn relapse triggers.]]
slides.sub: Why it hits so hard — and how to protect yourself.

slides.title: Pain wants [[numbing]]
slides.body: Rejection, loneliness, replaying everything. P*rn offers a quick escape from that pain — for about ten minutes.

slides.title: The [[rebound]] spiral
slides.body: Many people describe binging p*rn after a breakup to feel wanted or distracted. It usually leaves them feeling emptier, not better.

slides.title: Feel it, don't [[flee]] it
slides.body: Grief is supposed to hurt. Let it. Talk, write, train, cry — anything that processes it instead of numbing it with p*rn.

slides.title: Your breakup [[survival plan]]
items: Blocker on — this is a high-risk week for p*rn.
Tell a friend you're struggling.
Fill your evenings with people and plans.
Unfollow your ex for now.
slides.note: Did a breakup ever send you back to p*rn? Comment "me" 👇

slides.title:
Heal the heartbreak.
[[Skip the p*rn.]]
slides.lead: An AI coach for the hard nights, guided audio sessions and a panic button when p*rn urges hit.

carousels.name: Travel and hotel rooms: p*rn relapse risk

slides.title: Hotel room. Alone. New city. [[P*rn relapse waiting.]]
slides.sub: Why trips are so risky — and how to plan for them.

slides.title: No [[routine]]
slides.body: Your normal schedule, gym and people are all gone. Without structure, p*rn urges fill the empty hours.

slides.title: Total [[privacy]]
slides.body:
Nobody around, nobody expecting you, a new network that may skip your p*rn filters.

It's the perfect setup for a relapse.

slides.title: "What happens on the [[trip]]"
slides.body: The "it doesn't count when I'm away" thought is a trap. A p*rn binge on a trip still follows you home.

slides.title: Your travel [[plan]]
items: Check your p*rn blocker works on hotel Wi-Fi and mobile data.
Plan your evenings before you arrive.
Use the hotel gym or walk the city.
Check in daily with someone at home.
slides.note: Where do you travel most — work or family? 👇

slides.title:
Take your progress
[[everywhere.]]
slides.lead: A p*rn blocker that travels with your phone, daily check-ins and streaks that don't take vacations.

carousels.name: Can you just watch less p*rn?

slides.title: "I'll just watch less p*rn." [[Does moderation work?]]
slides.sub: An honest look at cutting back vs. quitting.

slides.title: Why it [[sounds]] good
slides.body:
Quitting p*rn completely feels extreme. "Less" feels doable.

For some people, it might be a first step.

slides.title: Why it often [[fails]]
slides.body: "Just once a week" needs you to make the right call while the p*rn urge is strongest. Many people find every "allowed" time restarts the cravings.

slides.title: The [[honest]] test
slides.body: Have you tried cutting back on p*rn before? Did it stick? If not, that's useful information — not a failure.

slides.title: Choose [[clearly]]
items: Decide in writing: moderation or quitting p*rn.
Set a time limit for the experiment — 30 days.
Track honestly what actually happens.
Switch to quitting if moderation keeps slipping.
slides.note: Moderation or full quit — which works for you? Comment M or Q 👇

slides.title:
Whatever you choose,
[[take control of p*rn.]]
slides.lead: Habit tracking that shows the honest truth, a p*rn blocker and support when urges hit.

slides.title: Moved somewhere new? [[P*rn fills the lonely nights fast.]]
slides.sub: How to settle in without a p*rn habit.

slides.title: No one [[knows]] you yet
slides.body: No friends nearby, empty weekends, nobody checking in. That's when many people say their p*rn use quietly doubled.

slides.title: Your own [[room]], finally
slides.body:
Total privacy feels like freedom.

But it also removes every brake that kept p*rn in check at home.

slides.title: Build your [[life]] first
slides.body: The faster you build real connections in a new place, the less space p*rn has. People are the best p*rn blocker.

slides.title: Your first [[30 days]]
items: Join one thing: a gym, sport, club or class.
Say yes to every reasonable invite.
Call home regularly.
Set up your p*rn blocker on day one.
slides.note: Recently moved? Where to? Say hi in the comments 👇

slides.title:
New city.
[[Same p*rn-free you.]]
slides.lead: An anonymous community, 1-on-1 accountability and a p*rn blocker for your new start.

carousels.name: Why you crave p*rn after a big win

slides.title: You got the job. Aced the exam. [[Then relapsed on p*rn.]]
slides.sub: Why good days can trigger p*rn too.

slides.title: The [[reward]] reflex
slides.body: "I earned this." Your brain wants to celebrate with the fastest reward it knows. For many people, that's still p*rn.

slides.title: Guard [[down]]
slides.body: On hard days you're on alert. On great days you relax — and stop watching for p*rn triggers. That's exactly when they get you.

slides.title: Plan the [[celebration]]
slides.body: Decide now how you'll celebrate wins: a meal out, a call home, something you've wanted. Give your brain a better reward than p*rn.

slides.title: Celebrate [[p*rn-free]]
items: Share the win with someone right away.
Do something physical — the energy has to go somewhere.
Treat yourself to a real reward.
Stay alert that night — blocker stays on.
slides.note: How will you celebrate your next win? Comment it 👇

slides.title:
Win the day.
[[Win against p*rn.]]
slides.lead: Streaks that make every p*rn-free day count, daily actions and a panic button for surprise urges.
